newsitem.title: UK: Brent slips as demand retreats, Urals weaker.
newsitem.headline: Brent slips as demand retreats, Urals weaker.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude weakened on Monday, pushed lower by ebbing February demand, traders said.

A Brent cargo due to load February 16-18 traded between European majors on Monday at March Brent +29 cents a barrel, slightly easier than a Brent loading February 12-14 that traded on Friday at March Brent +33 cents.
"There's a lack of interest. There is no need for the crude, and we are a couple of weeks away from the March programmes. It's going to be quiet until IP week," a trader said.
Softer values were reflected in the paper market, where Feb/March slid about 15 cents to +40/+50 while March/April traded twice at March +43, down from around March +45 on Friday.
Brent Contracts for Difference slipped around nine cents to March +23/+26 for Feb 3-7 dates, and around three cents to March +10/+12 for Feb 10-14.
Traders blamed the lower Brent levels on a retracement of last week's midweek rally.
Looming bearishly over the market is the fact that four of five Brent dates were five o'clocked on Friday.
"The market was looking top-heavy," one trader said.
Med traders said Urals was slipping amid ample availabilities of the Russian crude and other grades.
Talk of trade on Friday at Dated Brent -75 cents a barrel cif Genoa was denied but even potential sellers said it would be difficult to achieve that level this week.
"There are a couple of majors interested but they're looking for a discount in the 80s, at the best the high 70s," said one.
Traders said Monday's improvement in margins was likely to be short-lived with gas oil staying weak and offers of other regional grades were making life difficult for Urals sellers.
"There's some Syrian and Libyan on offer," said one.
